neighbours.label: An extent adverb that says how fully a state holds ('largely', 'almost completely', 'entirely'), not manner, time or frequency adverbs in the same slot.
fire: The old district was largely destroyed during the war.
Her early poems are almost completely forgotten today.
The success of the project was largely due to volunteers.
The island's economy depends almost entirely on tourism.
His theory was largely rejected by other scientists.
The forest has been almost completely cleared for farming.
The report is based entirely on public records.
The coastline stayed largely untouched until the 1970s.
quiet: The old district was suddenly destroyed during the war.
Her early poems are often read aloud today.
The success of the project was due on Friday.
The island's economy depends on the weather each year.
His theory was quickly rejected by other scientists.
The forest has been cleared again for farming.
The report is based in the city library.
The coastline was visited by tourists in the 1970s.
